profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Blizzard Entertainment
profile.summary:
Hey! I'm a C/C++ software engineer at Blizzard working in the Game Systems team. On that team, I write code for key miroservices that game teams implement into their games. 

Most notably, I am the primary owner of the Leaderboard service used in many of our games, and a secondary owner of the Account Migration, Data Protection, Notification, and Publication services.

positions.title: Associate Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Owner of the Leaderboards service that implements backend logic for game teams to use. Answering to game teams whenever there is a question on how the service works.
• Fixed bugs relating to Leaderboards and incorporated new APIs for game teams to use.
• Created a script to delete all data for an individual game from leaderboards in both staging and production environments.
• Owner of the Benefactor service overlooking PC bangs and the logic for time deduction and licenses.
• Secondary owner of the Session service which gates session creation/destruction and tracks metrics across a user's session.
• Drafted new design and architecture for the Publication service's handling of configuration files.
• Overhauled the notification configuration structure so that game teams can write better config files
• Helped convert internal service code from 32-bit account ids to 64-bit account ids while handling backwards compatibility issues as well as creating new tables for dual writing.
• Handled on-call live operations work to handle issues with varying severities.

positions.title: Software Engineer I
positions.description:
• Addressed bugs and added enhancements to Xcelium, a logic simulation for chip design verification used by over thousands of customers
• Developed a feature for Samsung that reported unsupported UPF commands during parsing using a combination of a hash table, linked lists, and bit manipulation
• Added tool capability at the request of ARM to allow for multiple isolation signals in the set_isolation UPF command
• Maintained and added to a new internal use feature for validating UPF isolation and retention
• Debugged and optimized codebase to fix any potential issues (off-by-one, referencing invalid index, memory allocation), reduce code duplication, and reduce memory usage
• Presented functional specifications to the R&D team, Product Validation team, and Product Engineering team

positions.title: Software Developer Intern
positions.description:
• Worked on a team of four to rewrite 20-year-old enterprise intranet search engine used over 250,000 times per month 
• Created ETL scripts and set up data pipeline to move data from Oracle to MongoDB and MongoDB to Elasticsearch 
• Created unit tests to ensure quality of data in ETL process 
• Worked with a UI/UX designer to weigh search results in order to rank most relevant search results 
• Coordinated with a frontend developer to set up data correctly to display on a webpage

positions.title: Analytical Services Developer
positions.description:
• Quickly learned Javascript, Bootstrap, and Jquery to create a webapp used to forecast net staffing to help with employee schedules 
• Used Impala and Hadoop to transfer large databases from a virtual machine 
• Gathered printed data from a sticker by using Microsoft’s OCR 
• Debugged legacy code that kept track of people’s asset holdings and the transfers of that asset 
• Redesigned Python 2 scripts to run on Python 3

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
• Working with other members of the Engaging Computing Group, added a mailing system on the iSENSE website using Ruby 
• Debugged issues on the iSENSE website using HTML, CSS, and Ruby 
• Taught middle school students as well as a college class how to create an application using MIT’s App Inventor 2
